renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: telomere_karyotype
  title: Telomeric repeats along sequences
  description: |-
    Each bar is a sequence of an assembly, drawn to its length and shaded in windows by the count of telomeric repeat copies, with one karyotype per assembly. It answers which sequences end in a telomere.
    How to read: a sequence that is dark at both ends is capped by telomeres at both sides, which is the signature of a complete chromosome. A sequence dark at one end only was broken at the other. Repeats in the middle of a sequence are an interstitial array or a repeat unit that is not the telomere.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tolkit/telomeric-identifier/main/README.md
  kind: ideogram
  roles:
    chrom: sequence
    start: start
    end: end
    value: repeats
    sample: genome
    chrom_length: sequence_length

- component: advanced_viz
  id: repeats_along_sequences
  title: Telomeric repeat counts per window
  description: |-
    Each point is a window along a sequence, with the count of telomeric repeat copies found in it, drawn per assembly. It answers where along a sequence the repeats pile up.
    How to read: peaks at the first and last windows mark the telomeres. A flat low track means no telomere was found, and a peak away from the ends is an internal repeat array. Pick one sequence at a time to read the ends.
    Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tolkit/telomeric-identifier/main/README.md
  kind: coverage_track
  config:
    color_by: sample
  roles:
    chromosome: sequence
    position: start
    end: end
    value: repeats
    sample: genome

- component: card
  title: Telomeric repeat copies
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total count of telomeric repeat copies in all windows, with the median and the largest window beside it, and the bar splits the copies by assembly. It answers how much telomeric repeat each assembly holds.
    How to read: a larger share means more telomeric sequence assembled. Compare with the number of sequences, because an assembly of many small pieces can hold many repeats without complete chromosomes.
  column: repeats
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: genome
  caption: copies, by assembly
  headline: true

- component: table
  title: Repeat windows
  description: |-
    Each row is a window of a sequence with the forward and reverse repeat counts, their sum, the repeat unit searched and the sequence length. It answers the exact counts behind the karyotype.
    How to read: sort by repeats to list the strongest windows, then check whether they sit at the start or the end of their sequence.
